name: TaskUpdate
title: Update Task
description: Fill a task already on the person's screen with values a workflow found
whenToUse: Show a workflow's findings in a template the person is already looking at: a page's company profile filled with research, a form filled with what was learned. It fills the task on screen in place rather than sending a new one into the conversation. Name the task by its URI and give the values its props take.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Upstream data. The config's templates read it; nothing is read from it directly.

outputs.name: task
outputs.description: The task and the values it was filled with: { ref, props }

task.title: Task
task.description: The task on screen, by its URI, such as unoverse://templates/acme/company-profile.

step.title: Step
step.description: The step to move it to as it is filled, such as company. Leave empty to fill it where it is.

props.title: Values
props.description: The values to fill it with, keyed by the part they fill, then by its props. Example: return { profile: { name: signal.enrich.company.name, people: signal.loop.done.collected } }

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: flow
package.packageFile:
# FLOW AS MANIFESTS, node by node.
#
# The one package that can migrate INCREMENTALLY, because it declares no credentials. The
# all-or-nothing rule that forced `aws-toolkit` and `cloudinary` to be split came entirely from
# the credential coexistence check (a node needs `credentials/<name>.yaml` in its own package,
# but that file alongside a code `registerCredential` is an error). With no credentials there is
# no conflict, and `src/index.ts` registers each node on its own line — so a node moves by
# writing its manifest and deleting those two lines.
#
# ONE HOST, AND ONLY THE PLATFORM'S OWN. For most of this package's life the list was empty,
# and that was not an omission: nothing here reached the network at all. TaskRunner is the
# exception and a narrow one. A task's half finished state is the platform's own record, kept
# as a paused run, so reading and writing it is a loopback call to the engine and never a
# vendor. The spatial package carries the same single entry for the same reason.
#
# The numeric form deliberately: the pattern rejects a bare "localhost", and the engine's
# address is built as `http://127.0.0.1:${ENGINE_PORT ?? 4101}` by the executor itself, so
# nothing here chooses the host. A wildcard would turn a flow package into a way to send a
# person's half written application somewhere else.
#
# WHAT IS STILL CODE, and why:
#
#   UMAP  runs umap-js IN PROCESS. Genuine local compute, reaching no host. Also of doubtful
#         value as written: it received ONE vector, faked a second by copying it with +0.0001
#         on every element so umap-js would run, and returned near-meaningless coordinates —
#         the real reduction lives in services/umap now. A candidate for removal, undecided.
#
#   SendObject  RETIRED to _legacy, user decision 2026-07-29 — it published to the live
#               session rather than answering the graph, and the `publish` capability that
#               replaced that lane (see Suggestions) covers the need.
#
# Suggestions, which used to sit on this list for the same reason as SendObject, is now a
# manifest: what actually needed code was one push into the caller's template state, and that
# is the executor's `publish` capability (api/publish.yaml) — declared under `requires` below.
#
# AND ONE REMOVAL rather than a migration. Gone from the catalog, so a saved workflow naming
# it now fails to resolve the type:
#
#   MCP             a generic schema-driven mcpService provider from before real service nodes
#                   existed. Superseded by UnoverseMCP in the engine and by per-vendor providers
#                   (HubspotMCP, SalesforceMCP, SlackMCP), so nothing needed it.
#
# FieldValidator was on this list, removed because its five outputs all derive from one
# properties-map cascade and expressions had no way to bind an intermediate value — the cascade
# had to be written out again inside every expression needing it; `completionPercentage` alone
# came to four copies. Named helpers (shared/helpers.yaml) are exactly that binding, so it is
# BACK, same type and connectors, and any workflow that named it resolves again.

name: flow
displayName: Flow
description: Control flow, routing and workflow annotation
version: 2.0.0
category: flow

allowedHosts:
  - 127.0.0.1
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Notes and documentation on the canvas
  - Branch, relay and read the running workflow's own context
  - Transform data inline, with optional content ids and run-scoped saved values
  - Loop over an array, running real workflow steps once per item
  - Validate collected data against a schema and get the next missing field to ask for
  - Walk a task's steps, handing out what is still outstanding and taking the answers back
  - Push suggested FAQs, actions and recommendations to the live chat UI
  - Fill a task already on the person's screen with a workflow's findings

requires:
  # 1.7.0 for named helpers (shared/helpers.yaml), which FieldValidator's emit rows call —
  # the same floor spatial set when helpers landed. Previously 1.5.0.
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  # TaskRunner's calls to the engine, and to the platform's MCP when it loads a task by URI:
  # `headers` because the MCP session id arrives in one. Declared for the same reason as
  # everything else here: the package says which capabilities its nodes need, so an install
  # against an executor without them fails at install rather than at run.
  transport: [json, headers]
  # Code's "Save to Context" toggle. Declared even though it cannot silently no-op the way a cache
  # read can — an executor without `save` throws rather than shrugging — because the reason to
  # declare is the same either way: the package says which platform capabilities its nodes need, so
  # installing it against an older executor fails at install rather than at run.
  state:
    - save
  # The LoopStart/LoopEnd pair. More is at stake in declaring these than in most capabilities: an
  # executor that cannot keep an index does not iterate, so an install that skipped this check would
  # run a loop body exactly once and report success.
  loop:
    - open
    - read
    - advance
  # Suggestions' whole job, and TaskRunner's position on screen (tasks.<ref>). Declared because
  # on an executor without the publish lane the node would emit its connector and never reach
  # the screen — "worked" everywhere except the one place it matters.
  publish: true

files.api/events.yaml:
# NO CALLS. The engine resolves every config field before the node runs, so the task and its
# values are emitted as they are and pushed to the screen by api/publish.yaml.

- emit: task
  value: "return { ref: config.task, step: config.step || undefined, props: config.props }"
files.api/publish.yaml:
# THE TASK ON SCREEN, FILLED IN PLACE (SIGNAL.md 6c). Merged into the caller's app state under
# `tasks.<ref>`: `props`, and `step` when one is given, the same step TaskRunner publishes
# there; a template the page draws with that URI moves to the step and merges each part's values
# into that part.
# `output.task`, so the screen and the graph never drift.

when: "return !!(output.task && output.task.ref && output.task.props && typeof output.task.props === 'object')"
data: "return { tasks: { [output.task.ref]: output.task.step ? { step: output.task.step, props: output.task.props } : { props: output.task.props } } }"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [task, props]
  properties:
    task:
      type: string
      title: Task
      description: >-
        The task on screen, by its URI, such as unoverse://templates/acme/company-profile.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    step:
      type: string
      title: Step
      description: >-
        The step to move it to as it is filled, such as company. Leave empty to fill it
        where it is.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    props:
      type: object
      title: Values
      description: >-
        The values to fill it with, keyed by the part they fill, then by its props. Example:
        return { profile: { name: signal.enrich.company.name, people: signal.loop.done.collected } }
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [task, step, props]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: >-
      Upstream data. The config's templates read it; nothing is read from it directly.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: task
    type: object
    description: "The task and the values it was filled with: { ref, props }"
files.node.yaml:
type: TaskUpdate
kind: PromiseNode

name: Update Task
category: Output
color: "#8B5CF6"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: Fill a task already on the person's screen with values a workflow found

whenToUse: >-
  Show a workflow's findings in a template the person is already looking at: a page's company
  profile filled with research, a form filled with what was learned. It fills the task on
  screen in place rather than sending a new one into the conversation. Name the task by its
  URI and give the values its props take.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A push to a live screen is a side effect, and a cached one silently stops happening.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# Every field arrives already resolved, so the fixture supplies finished values. With no live
# session the publish no-ops; the emitted task is what is checked.
testData:
  config:
    task: unoverse://templates/acme/company-profile
    step: profile
    props:
      profile:
        name: Acme
        summary: A test company.
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    task: "return output.task.ref === 'unoverse://templates/acme/company-profile' && output.task.step === 'profile' && output.task.props.profile.name === 'Acme'"
